title: A repeat student-debt-relief refund is conditioned on prior cashing and payment exposure without proving debt correction
source_unit: FTC Mission Hills Federal student-loan-debt-relief refund program and second-payment route
geography: United States consumers affected by Mission Hills Federal and related student-loan-debt-relief practices

denominator.unit: people reported as receiving a second-round check after cashing the first check and paying defendants more than $430

second_round_total.unit: more than U.S. dollars in second-round checks

first_round_total.unit: more than U.S. dollars in first-round refunds sent in March 2024

recipient_condition.value: cashed the first check and paid the defendants more than $430
recipient_condition.unit: administrative eligibility condition for the second round

underlying_exposure.value: FTC reported upfront fees and false promises about lowering or eliminating student-loan payments, without applying collected money to balances or obtaining forgiveness

second_check_receipt_and_recovery.unit: missing second-check delivery, cashing, debt-balance correction, residual fees, adequacy, and household recovery

observations.method: Bounded extraction from the official FTC Mission Hills refund page; first-round refunds, prior cashing, second-round dispatch, and debt-recovery outcomes are kept as separate stages.
observations.uncertainty: The public page does not provide the full harmed denominator, individual amounts, first-check cashing rate, second-check cashing, debt-balance correction, residual loss, household adaptation, trust, switching, or exit. A recipient-conditioned second payment is not a recovery rate for all affected borrowers.
observations.subgroup: People who paid the defendants more than $430 and cashed the first refund check; no socioeconomic, loan-balance, or subgroup outcome is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: Prior check cashing makes the second-round population more reachable, but the condition can exclude people who never received, could not access, or could not cash the first payment; the payment also does not establish that a student-loan balance was corrected.

related_sources.claim: The FTC refund index lists Mission Hills Federal as an official refund program.
The FTC describes prior payment cashing, address updates, reissue, and additional-payment stages in its refund process.

boundary: This record establishes a student-debt-relief enforcement and recipient-conditioned second-refund route. It does not establish second-payment receipt, cashing, debt correction, adequate recovery, household security, trust, switching, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the official FTC refund page HTML retrieved through the search.ftc.gov mirror for extraction.
